meta.title: A Note Before the Long Walk

paragraphs: Posted by Lily. Nurse Jill wrote a note for the families before the Explorers' long walk. Teacher Kim gave a copy to each child, and now it is on the blog too. Please read it with your family.

Dear families, On Saturday, the Explorers will take a long walk in the nature park. The walk is two hours long, and we will stop often. We leave the school at eight o'clock, and we come back at noon. Exercise is good for children, but a long walk may cause small problems. Please read the signs below, and talk about them with your child.

A child may feel pain in the legs or the feet. A small pain is normal after a long walk, but a strong pain is not normal. In that case, the child must tell Teacher Kim and rest on a bench. The group will wait, and nobody must walk fast. If the pain stays for more than one day, please make an appointment with a doctor. Please do not give a strong medicine without a doctor's advice.

A child may fall and cut a knee. A little blood is not a danger. Teacher Kim has a first-aid box, and she will wash the cut with clean water. Then she will put a bandage on the knee. The child can walk again after a short rest. If the blood does not stop after ten minutes, she will call you immediately. Please keep your phone near you on Saturday.

Please pack a healthy lunch for your child. Water is the best drink for the walk. Rice, fruit, and a bottle of water are a good choice. Please do not pack sweet drinks. Does your child have an allergy to nuts, eggs, or milk? Check the ingredients of every food in the lunch box. The signs of an allergy are red spots, itchy skin, or a sore stomach. If a child has trouble with breathing, there is danger. We will call an adult at once.

Please give your child a hat and sunscreen, and add two pairs of socks. Old shoes are not good for a long walk. Good shoes are important, because they stop many foot problems. We will have fun. Thank you for your help, and have a good walk. Best wishes, Nurse Jill.
